@@ -24,2 +24,4 @@
 
+Creator input passes physical player coordinates through `core/display-transform.ts`: float32 matrices, signed twip translations, device-pixel mouse rounding, and the event-target/stage/reference Point conversions. The browser supplies the applied CSS transform and DPR; the numeric module has no DOM or saved-data access. `EditorPositions` separately owns transient clip x/y. Drawing, hit tests, selection bounds and radial validation consume those getters, while tank codes and history retain raw saved coordinates. Drag membership/twin links update during movement and selected positions synchronize on release. Nudging advances both stores independently per frame; undo and rejected edits reconstruct clips from accepted metadata. Class measurement separately constructs its source snapshot from saved coordinates through position setters.
+
 Attached status marks are simulation state: their chosen part positions, rotations, variants, and replacement lifetime stay stable across frames and inactive fields. `SwfTankStatusView` consumes those choices without drawing random values or changing game rules. It holds variant frames while allowing nested clips to animate and applies the recovered infection color matrix to the complete tank view. Screen ink is an independently queued global effect; its lifetime and overlap do not belong to an avatar.

## Creator event coordinates and independent saved/display positions

- The source's selection handlers read "'`MouseEvent.stageX/stageY`, convert through `_‑6H.globalToLocal`, and write each delivered delta through `clip.x/y` before saving the next cursor. Palette `_‑Zl/_‑8a` also reads stage-event Points through `movTank.globalToLocal`; `StopLibraryDrag` commits the last moved pose. The earlier eighth-pixel browser assertion did not establish that contract. Input now follows the float32 matrix and signed-twip conversions, including device-pixel rounding and the target/stage/reference round trips. Each display write truncates independently. Matrix Point products use nearest/ties-even instead. The applied CSS scale supplies the view matrix; a painted bounding box can differ by about0.00003px at1.3×.
- `select_mc` is creator969'"'s depth123 sprite867, at3719/4634twips with unit scale, zero alpha and cached bitmap. Its child866 has bounds±3500twips. The reference sprites and tank share the rings registration. A pinned Ruffle source revision ("'`89a7049965f3090e706265670df309a5128233ac`, principally `core/src/display_object.rs`, `render/src/matrix.rs`, MouseEvent getters and `swf/src/types/twips.rs`) supplies the numeric semantic guide. The observed WASM imports offsetX/offsetY and DPR as f64; an integer JavaScript/WASM import was not the cause. Matching loaded bytes does not prove that revision built the observed runtime.
- The original exports demonstrate more than final quarter-pixel movement. At4×, positive and negative eighth-pixel gestures can respectively leave x−20 unchanged and move it to−20.25. At3×, three thirds move−20.25 to−19.2. Fractional placement exports include x−40.35/y±10.3 and, at1.3×, x−50/y±10. Fifteen numeric goldens cover ten drag sequences across DPR1/2 and five palette placements at scales1/1.3/3/4; the DPR2 drag set also uses1.5×. Fresh captures with Chrome157/Ruffle0.7.1 reproduced all15 earlier exports, with64 foreground captures and no observed page errors. Loaded JavaScript/WASM identities were independently observed. These are bounded emulation observations, not Adobe execution or a whole-frame comparison.
- Source `arrTankDetails` stores raw imported/saved coordinates separately from display clips. Loading and undo construct clips through position setters without rewriting raw metadata. Nudges update raw x and the clip getter independently, including per-frame Number addition. Drag release copies selected surviving clip positions back; twin membership/link changes occur during dragging. `EditorPositions` now owns that transient display state, with separate saved/display observations for browser verification. Drawing, alpha hit tests, marquee geometry, outlines and `_‑6k` radial checks use display getters. `UpdateClass` instead builds fresh measurement clips from saved metadata. Rotation/scale controls preserve saved positions, and rejected edits rebuild the accepted display state.
- The capture tool now accepts `precision` and `placement` scenarios and `BT3_REFERENCE_DPR=1|2`. With an owned reference server on3104 and the player'"'s local SWF, capture the three directories below and regenerate the numeric fixture. Only numerical event/export data and identities enter the fixture; SWF/media/screenshots remain local and ignored.

BT3_REFERENCE_PORT=3104 bun tools/reference-player.ts
# In a separate terminal; set BT3_SWF_FILE to your local file for each capture.

BT3_REFERENCE_SCENARIO=precision BT3_REFERENCE_DPR=2 BT3_REFERENCE_CAPTURE_DIR=reference-captures/creator-point-precision/tracked-reproduction/original-dpr2 bun tools/capture-creator-reference.ts

bun tools/import-creator-point-reference.ts reference-captures/creator-point-precision/tracked-reproduction
bun run format
```

- Limits: the saved/display ownership path is established by decompiled source and recreation save-code/nudge/drag/undo tests; a controlled original fractional-code-import differential remains open. The measured input targets are the workspace selection overlay and valid palette destinations. Arbitrary child/widget targets, other DPR/scales, letterboxed/shaken parent configurations, complete scale/rotation getter precision, constructor/RNG/event timing and full creator/Adobe parity remain unproved. Ordinary native/original boss-win playthrough and the full recreation goal remain incomplete.
EOF

input.title: Match creator input precision and saved/display coordinates
input.body:
## Summary

Match the original creator’s small drags and placements while preserving raw saved coordinates.

```text
Physical pointer → source matrix/Point conversions → display x/y writes
Import / untouched save → retain raw metadata
Nudge → update raw metadata and display getters independently per frame
Drag release → copy selected display positions into saved metadata
Undo / rejection → restore metadata and reconstruct display clips
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** public browser baselines differed from original exports in10of20 drag cases; fractional deltas remained raw instead of passing through the source input/display conversions.
  **After:**15 original numeric goldens cover ten drag sequences across DPR1/2 and five fractional palette placements. Actual mock/native browser replays match20 drag and10 placement results exactly.
- Fresh unmodified-original captures reproduced all15 exports with Chrome157/Ruffle0.7.1,64 foreground captures and no observed page errors. The capture scenarios and numeric-fixture importer are repeatable; the fixture contains coordinates and loaded-module identities.
- A fractional imported x7.125 displays at7.1 and survives an untouched saved-code round trip. Nudging retains8.125/8.1 independently; drag release synchronizes the displayed pose; undo restores raw metadata. Class snapshots reconstruct from saved metadata, while radial validation uses current clips.
- Formatting, TypeScript, **794 unit tests /7,621 assertions**, production build and **28 affected browser cases without skips** pass with the supplied SWF. Coverage includes source pointer replays, saved/display ownership, merge/respawn, zero-delta input, selection, painted outlines, sliders, rejection and save routes. Placement screenshots were inspected in both asset modes.
- The original fractional-code-import differential, arbitrary widget targets, other scale/DPR and letterboxed/shaken-parent comparisons, full scale/rotation getter precision and Adobe/full-game parity remain open. Static source ownership and bounded runtime comparisons have distinct evidence limits, recorded in the fidelity ledger. Artwork and capture files remain local.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

No save-schema migration, dependency or workflow changes.

**Blast Radius:** creator

Pointer conversion, per-write positions, transient display ownership and editor geometry/class checks change together. Raw serialized coordinates retain the source caller-specific behavior.
